clue.text: Urgent appeal about a newspaper that's deceitful

indicators.note: the appeal goes round the outside of the other pieces, so about signals a container

parts.note: a cry is an urgent appeal or plea
FT is the Financial Times, a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone's desperate plea concerning a newspaper turns out to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Urgent appeal' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'that's deceitful' at the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crafty person is cunning and sly, ready to trick others, which is to be deceitful.

clue.text: Writer of document perhaps making PM recoil

indicators.note: the letters of PM and recoil are made into something new, so making signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A clerk drafts a paper that makes the Prime Minister flinch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoil' looks like the anagram signal but it is fodder; 'making' rearranges PM plus RECOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who assembles a document, such as a report or dictionary, is its compiler, a kind of writer.

clue.text: Tool used by trawlermen

indicators.note: the tool sits inside the word trawlermen, used by it as part of its spelling

explanation.surface: Fishermen on a trawler have a particular implement they rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' signals the letters inside tr-AWL-ermen.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Wave from chap got up in new suit

indicators.note: the reversed chap sits within the rearranged suit, so in signals a container
a new version of suit is the same letters in a fresh order
in a down clue, a word got up is read from bottom to top, so it is turned round

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A man stands up in a new suit and a wave of attention follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' makes a reversal because this is a down clue; 'new' makes TSUI from the fodder; 'in' does the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake or undersea upheaval.

clue.text: Industrial action attendant on good man getting work

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a good man
OP is short for opus, a work
a page is a young attendant or servant

explanation.surface: A page boy accompanies a saintly figure who is busy at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Industrial action' is the definition: a strike in which work stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a strike or walkout, a halt in work as industrial action by employees.

clue.text: Disturbance of giant rainstorm passing from a one place to another

definitions.text: passing from a one place to another

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A huge storm disrupts travel between places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbance of' rearranges the fourteen letters of GIANT RAINSTORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmigration is movement from one place or state to another, especially of a soul passing into a new body.

clue.text: Example of jargon that's new

parts.note: patter is the glib talk or lingo of a trade

explanation.surface: A specimen of insider talk that has just been coined.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or example to be followed or copied.

clue.text: Greatly surprising when fashion is the centre of things

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as she came in'
ton is an old word for the height of fashion

indicators.note: only the middle letters of things are taken

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed that style has become the focus of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' takes HING from t-HING-s.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing is amazing, so remarkable it greatly surprises people.

clue.text: Bury cat in section of garden bed

indicators.note: the cat is put within the piece of letters, so in signals a container
a section of the words garden bed is a run of letters across them

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Someone buries a pet cat in part of a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures burying a pet; 'section of' takes a run of letters across two words, and 'in' does the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, so to bury it.

clue.text: Outstanding leader, but one who's below par?

definitions.meaning: a leading figure in a movement or cause, the one at its forefront
par as a standard; one who stands below a standard, holding it up, carries it

explanation.surface: A star leader, yet one who seems to fall short of the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Par is a standard, and someone below a flag holds it up: the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the soldier carrying a regiment's flag, the term now means a prominent leader of a movement.

clue.text: Person who is timid and quiet, almost disastrously

indicators.note: something done disastrously goes badly wrong, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A shy person speaks so softly that it nearly ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like a cue to drop a letter but it is fodder; 'disastrously' rearranges QUIET plus ALMOST.
explanation.definitionFit: A milquetoast is a meek, timid, spineless person, named after a cartoon character.

clue.text: Nearly closed? Time for a quick drink

parts.note: a door pushed to is shut or almost shut

explanation.surface: With the bar almost shut, it is time for a swift drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Pushing a door 'to' leaves it closed or nearly so.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, a quick drink.

clue.text: Make a habit at home to take cereal

parts.note: someone at home is in
grain is a cereal crop such as wheat

explanation.surface: Eating breakfast cereal at home becomes a routine.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingrain something is to fix it deeply, so it becomes a fixed habit.

clue.text: Serious Australian gets part in Hamlet

parts.note: grave means serious or solemn
digger is slang for an Australian, especially a soldier

explanation.surface: A solemn Australian actor lands a role in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet the gravedigger is a comic role, joking while digging Ophelia's grave.
explanation.definitionFit: The gravedigger is a character, a role or part, in Shakespeare's Hamlet.

clue.text: Problem involving bird's breastbone

indicators.note: the problem wraps round the bird, so involving signals a container

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a bird's chest bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat bone at the front of the chest, the breastbone.

clue.text: For instance, landed man is upset about a state belief in equality

indicators.note: here about means alongside, placing the jumbled letters next to A and the state

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for instance
alit is an old past tense of alight, meaning landed
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A landowner, say, is disturbed by a state doctrine that everyone is equal.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island is the US state; 'upset' rearranges the five letters of the man-is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Egalitarianism is the doctrine that all people are equal and deserve equal rights.

clue.text: What one gets from a layer of paint

definitions.text: What one gets from a layer of paint

parts.words: What one gets from a layer of paint
parts.note: a layer is a hen that lays, giving the casing of what it lays; it is also a semi-matt paint finish

explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is both the hard casing a hen produces and a type of low-sheen paint finish.

clue.text: Never before seen outcome of a slipped disc?

definitions.meaning: a disc is a record, and one that slips from the hand may break

explanation.surface: An unprecedented result from someone's back injury.
explanation.walkthrough: A slipped disc suggests a back injury, but a disc is a gramophone record that might smash.
explanation.definitionFit: A record-breaking feat beats every previous one, so it is unprecedented.

clue.text: Coal pit is out of sight

indicators.note: something out is wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coal mine has vanished from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sight' reads as one phrase, but 'of sight' is the definition and 'is out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to vision, so it describes things of sight.

clue.text: A state without structure

parts.note: a condition of a society lacking any government or order, rather than a nation

explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is lawlessness, the absence of government or order in a society.

clue.text: Jerk about, hard?

parts.note: a twit is a fool or jerk
C is short for circa, about
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to jolt something around forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sudden jerky movement while its words build the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden small jerk of a muscle or body part.

clue.text: Instrument that's sometimes piercing suit

definitions.meaning: a small blown device giving a shrill, penetrating note

explanation.surface: A musical instrument with a shrill sound cuts through a set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, a London dialect, uses whistle and flute for suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistle is a small instrument with a shrill sound, and Cockney slang for a suit.

clue.text: Hardened criminal conceals heroin in boat

parts.note: a thug is a violent criminal

explanation.surface: A tough criminal smuggles drugs aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' hides the H from THUG, leaving the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tug is a small powerful boat that tows larger vessels.

clue.text: Repetitive movement in C?

parts.note: C as the chemical symbol for an element, whose circulation through nature repeats; not a musical key

explanation.definitionFit: The carbon cycle is the continuous circulation of carbon through the atmosphere, living things and the earth.

clue.text: Hazelnut loaf

definitions.meaning: a cobnut is a kind of hazelnut

explanation.definitionFit: A cob is a hazelnut, and also a small round loaf of bread.

clue.text: Study of arms left on goddess that's boringly academic?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods
dry describes dull, scholarly writing

explanation.surface: A subject concerning weapons, linked to a goddess, proves tediously scholarly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons but means coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry is the study of coats of arms and their design.

clue.text: Representative figure throws up over my back

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read backwards
the throws go over, round the outside of, my

parts.note: to lob is to throw something up high
taken as written

explanation.surface: A delegate hurls things over someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets my inside the throws, making LOBMYS; 'back' turns that whole run round.
